Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to JSW Infrastructure Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Investec Capital Services Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines 
will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Veenit Pasad from Investec Capital Services. Thank you, 
and over to you, sir. 
Veenit Pasad: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone. A warm welcome on behalf of Investec India to the Q2 
FY27 earnings call of JSW Infrastructure Limited. We have with us the Senior Management 
team from the company represented by; Mr. Rinkesh Roy, Joint MD and CEO; Mr. Nagarajan, 
CFO; and Mr. Vishesh Pachnanda, Head Investor Relations. 
Now I'll hand over the call to senior management for their opening remarks, post which we'll 
open the floor for Q&A. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Rinkesh Roy: 
Thank you, Veenit. Good evening, everyone and thank you for joining us for our earnings call 
to discuss our performance for the quarter and half year ended September 30th, 2026. The global 
operating environment continues to remain dynamic, shaped by geopolitical developments, 
evolving trade flows and periodic supply chain disruptions. Despite these uncertainties, India's 
economic fundamentals remain strong, supported by robust domestic demand, continued 
investments in infrastructure, manufacturing-led growth and favorable policy initiatives. 
As India's logistics and trade ecosystem continues to evolve, we believe the long-term 
opportunity for integrated ports and logistics infrastructure remains highly compelling. Against 
this backdrop, JSW Infrastructure delivered another period of healthy operational performance 
and strategic progress during the first half of FY27. 
During H1 FY27, we handled 60.5 million tonnes of cargo, including 29.4 million tonnes in Q2, 
and our India operations grew 10% year-on-year, significantly ahead of industry growth of 5%, 
driven by a diversified cargo mix, deeper customer engagement and increasing third-party cargo 
volumes. 
The resilience of our operating model and the strategic positioning of our assets enabled us to 
maintain strong momentum across our network. In our India operations, third-party volumes 
reached 28.1 million tonnes, registering growth of 11% year-on-year, despite a decline of 1% 
due to the nil contribution from Fujairah Liquid Terminal.

A key pillar of our growth strategy continues to be logistics, where we are rapidly building a 
pan-India integrated platform. Navkar Corporation delivered another strong performance during 
the period, with domestic cargo volumes growing 26% year-on-year and EXIM cargo volumes 
increasing 7% year-on-year in H1 '27. 
We also continued to strengthen our logistics platform during the period. Our rail rake fleet 
expanded from 42 rakes in Q1 FY27 to 78 rakes currently, reflecting the rapid scale-up of our 
logistics business. We remain on track to further increase the fleet to at least 110 rakes by March 
'27. 
The logistics business continues to benefit from increased network utilization and customer 
additions. Overall, on a consolidated basis, our operating revenue was INR2,926 crores for the 
first half of FY27, representing 18% year-on-year growth. Operating EBITDA for the period 
stood at INR1,348 crores, marking a 13% increase, while net profit reached INR686 crores. 
Turning to project execution during the quarter, we continued to make steady progress across 
our development pipeline. Execution remains on track across all major projects, with the slurry 
pipeline project reaching a significant milestone through the completion of approximately 257 
kilometers of pipeline lowering and another 10 kilometers of HDD pipelines in progress, 
equivalent to nearly 88% of the total scope. The project remains on schedule for commissioning 
by March '27. 
At Jatadhar Port, Odisha, construction activities are progressing at a healthy pace. Our 
brownfield expansion projects are also progressing steadily. At Dharamtar Port and Jaigarh Port, 
the berth side works are substantially completed and mechanization works are expected to be 
completed during Q1 FY28 for Jaigarh, while Dharamtar will be completed by Q4 '27. These 
investments will further enhance capacity, improve operational efficiencies and support future 
cargo growth. 
In the container cargo segment, we achieved a key milestone by signing the 30-year concession 
agreement for the 13 million ton per annum Outer Container Terminal project at NSD Dock, 
Kolkata. Once operational, the project will increase our total container handling capacity in 
Kolkata to approximately 1.4 million TEUs, significantly strengthening our presence in Eastern 
India, enhancing our container cargo volumes and enhancing our ability to serve the trade. 
During the quarter, we also commenced interim operations at the 6.3 million ton per annum 
Kolkata container terminal, which was awarded in JulY25, providing an early platform to 
establish customer relationships, build volumes and support a seamless transition to full-scale 
operations. 
Beyond ports, we continued to strengthen our logistics platform during the period through the 
acquisition of NCR Rail Infrastructure Limited, approval for the development of an inland 
container depot at Kudathini, Ballari and the award of the Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal at 
Kulipalaiyam, Tamil Nadu. 
These milestones further expanded our network footprint, enhanced our rail-link logistics 
infrastructure and strengthened our ability to deliver integrated end-to-end supply chain

solutions. These achievements build upon the strong progress made since our entry into logistics 
in October '24. 
In just two years, we have expanded our network from 3 locations to 8 locations across India, 
scaled our rake fleet nearly tenfold from 8 to 78 rakes and increased our domestic container fleet 
from approximately 2,400 containers to nearly 5,000 containers. This rapid scale-up reflects our 
commitment to building a nationwide multimodal logistics franchise and reinforces our vision 
of creating a leading integrated ports and logistics platform. 
Our long-term vision remains unchanged. We continue to build a diversified ports and logistics 
platform with a clear objective of expanding port capacity from the current 186 million tonnes 
per annum to 300 million tonnes by FY28 and further to 400 million tonnes by FY '30, while 
simultaneously creating a nationwide logistics network that enhances cargo stickiness, 
strengthens customer engagement and drives sustainable growth. 
As part of our strategy, we remain focused on the rapid scale-up of our logistics business while 
maintaining strong execution across our port expansion projects. With a strengthened balance 
sheet, a visible growth pipeline and increasing integration between our ports and logistics 
businesses, we are well positioned to capitalize on India's long-term trade and infrastructure 
opportunities and deliver sustainable value creation. 
With that, I would now like to hand over the call to our CFO, Mr. Nagarajan, who will take you 
through the financial performance and other details. Thank you. 
Nagarajan J: 
Thank you, Rinkesh ji, and good evening, everybody. Let me first talk about our port business. 
In Q2 FY27, the company handled cargo volumes of 29.4 million tonnes compared to 28.9 
million tonnes in Q2 FY26, registering a growth of 2% Y-o-Y, while our India operations grew 
by 8% Y-o-Y. 
The increase was primarily driven by improved capacity utilization at Paradip Coal Terminal, 
Ennore Bulk and Mangalore Coal terminals and was further contributed by interim operations 
at the Tuticorin Port and commencement of interim operations at the Kolkata container terminal. 
The overall growth was muted on account of nil of volume contribution from the Fujairah Liquid 
Terminal, along with lower volumes at Jaigarh and Paradip Iron Ore Terminal.  
The third-party cargo volumes accounted for 45% of the total volumes during the period. Third-
party volumes in the Indian business registered a healthy growth of 13% Y-o-Y. However, 
overall third-party volume growth was limited to 1% due to nil contribution from Fujairah 
terminal. 
Operating revenue for the ports segment grew by 9% during the quarter to INR1,202 crores, 
compared with INR1,100 crores in Q2 FY26. The revenue increase was driven by volume 
growth and ancillary and allied services, along with rupee depreciation.  
Operational EBITDA for the port segment stood at INR594 crores, up from INR585 crores. The 
EBITDA margin was 49.4% versus 53.1% a year ago, the dip in port EBITDA margin was 
primarily driven by absence of volume, contribution from Fujairah and incremental volumes

Terminals. 
Talking about logistics, Navkar Corp delivered strong operational and financial performance in 
Q2 FY27. Domestic cargo volumes stood at 459,000 metric tonnes, up 16% compared with the 
same period last year, while EXIM volumes reached 88,000 TEUs, representing 12% Y-o-Y 
growth. 
Operating EBITDA for the logistics segment stood at INR81 crores, up from INR25 crores, 
representing a 3.3x increase Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin expanded to 29% from 15%, driven by the 
growing contribution from rail logistics business. 
The rail rake fleet increased from 42 rakes at the beginning of the quarter to 78 rakes by quarter-
end. The base fleet of 42 rakes operated throughout the quarter, while out of the additional 36 
rakes, only 8 were deployed in September 2026.  
Consequently, 72 rakes have been operational since October, with the remaining 6 expected to 
be operationalized during November and December, providing further support to volume and 
earnings growth. A further 32 rakes are expected to be delivered over H2, which would take the 
total fleet size to 110 by March 2027. 
Total consolidated operating revenue for the company stood at INR1,481 crores and operating 
EBITDA stood at INR674 crores, reflecting a Y-o-Y growth of 17% and 11%, respectively. 
Consolidated depreciation was INR175 crores, and finance cost was INR108 crores in the 
current quarter, as compared to INR149 crores and INR99 crores, respectively, in the previous 
quarter ended September '25. 
PBT stood at INR431 crores, compared with INR463 crores in the corresponding period last 
year. The decline was primarily driven by unrealized forex losses on account of rupee 
depreciation, an upward shift in yield curve and higher depreciation charges, reflecting the 
commissioning of growth projects in the port business and the continued scale-up of the logistics 
segment. The impact on PBT was partially offset by higher other income during the period. 
PAT stood at INR328 crores, compared with INR369 crores in the corresponding period last 
year. The decline was primarily driven by lower PBT and higher effective tax rate, largely due 
to the absence of tax-exempt earnings from the Fujairah Oil Terminal during the period. 
As of September 2026, we maintained a cash position of INR1,693 crores, underscoring one of 
the strongest balance sheets in the sector. In line with the accounting treatment for the specialized 
rakes business, we have revised the FY27 logistics EBITDA margin guidance to 28% from 24%, 
while retaining the overall logistics EBITDA target of INR400 crores. 
Capex. The company has incurred a cumulative capex outlay of approximately INR8,250 crores 
up to September '26, including INR1,500 crores spent during the quarter towards ongoing and 
existing growth projects. In addition, the company has already committed a further INR6,000 
crores of capex by placing orders for machinery, long-lead items and other civil work towards
